# YouTube Tools - SEO brief

> **SERP-replacement risk: API.** Depends on YouTube data. Defend with formats, search, timestamps, export.

**Constraint:** no backlink building, no directory submissions. Everything else must be
perfect, because on-page and technical quality is the *only* lever being pulled. Give Google
no reason to prefer the incumbent.

> ⚠ **Iron rules in `BRIEF.md` apply here too — read them first.** Never write library code
> from memory: fetch current docs via **context7 MCP** for Astro/Tailwind/npm, the
> `cloudflare` and `wrangler` skills for Cloudflare, and `modern-web-guidance` for web
> platform APIs. Latest **stable**, never bleeding edge. Docs beat memory, always.

---

# ★ THE FOUR MUST-HAVES

**No SEO = no traffic = no money.** Nothing else in this document matters if these four are
missing. Ship none of them late.

| | Must-have | Means | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🏷 | **Meta tags** | Unique `<title>`, meta description, **OG image** on every page | §4 |
| ⚡ | **Speed = rank** | **100 PageSpeed score** | §2 |
| H1 | **On-page** | **Exactly one `<h1>`**, alt text on every image, clean URLs | §4 |
| 📄 | **Sitemap + schema** | `sitemap-index.xml`, `robots.txt`, **FAQ JSON-LD** | §6, §7 |

> **On the 100 score:** aim for 100 in Lighthouse, but **a 100 lab score does not guarantee
> passing field data**. The number that actually ranks you is CrUX at the 75th percentile —
> see §2. Treat 100 as the floor you build to, not the finish line.

---

## 1. The thing that actually decides survival

Not AI Overviews. **SERP-widget replacement.**

AI Overviews now appear on 47–64% of queries and cut informational traffic 20–40% — but
they hit *informational* intent. An AI Overview cannot test someone's mouse, read their
webcam, or open their SVG. **Tool queries are structurally protected.**

The real threat is proven inside this research: seed 16 (`hex to rgb`) is dead because Google
renders a colour picker directly in the SERP. Zero clicks, regardless of ranking.

**Rule: the more the tool depends on the visitor's own hardware, file, or live target, the
safer it is.** Read the risk tier at the top of this file. If it says `STRING` or `LIVE
FETCH`, depth is not optional — it is the moat. Batch mode, export, history, explanation,
and edge cases are what a SERP widget will never do.

## 2. Core Web Vitals — non-negotiable numbers

Targets at the **75th percentile of real users** (CrUX field data, not Lighthouse lab):

| Metric | Good | Target here |
|---|---|---|
| **LCP** Largest Contentful Paint | < 2.5s | **< 1.2s** |
| **INP** Interaction to Next Paint | < 200ms | **< 100ms** |
| **CLS** Cumulative Layout Shift | < 0.1 | **0** |

CWV is a *tiebreaker*, not a primary ranking factor — but a tiebreaker is exactly the
position you are in against near-equal incumbents, and the **March 2026 core update
increased performance weighting**. Aim well inside the thresholds so field data never drifts
out.

**How to hit it with the portfolio stack:**

- Astro static output. **Zero JS on first paint** — the tool hydrates as an island.
- LCP element is text or an inline SVG, never a web font or a remote image.
- **Self-host fonts**, `font-display: optional`, subset to used glyphs. Or use a system stack.
- Every image: explicit `width`/`height`, `loading="lazy"` below the fold,
  `fetchpriority="high"` on the LCP element, AVIF/WebP.
- **Reserve space for the tool** with `min-height` or `aspect-ratio` — a tool that pops in
  is the #1 source of CLS on pages like these.
- No layout-shifting ad slots above the fold. Reserve every ad container's exact height.
- Inline critical CSS; defer everything else.
- No third-party JS before interactive. Analytics loads last.

**Verify with field data, not lab scores.** A 100 Lighthouse score with bad CrUX means nothing.

## 3. Page architecture and internal linking

**One page per distinct intent — not per trivial variant.**

- Modifier variants (`X online`, `free X`, `X tool`, `X website`) → **same page**. Google
  treats them as one query; separate pages cannibalise each other.
- Synonyms describing a genuinely different job → **own page** (`double click test` is a
  different job from `polling rate test`).
- Check the SERP for two phrases: **if the same pages rank for both, one page serves both.**

**Structure:**

```
/                     primary head term, the main tool, above the fold
/<secondary-tool>/    each absorbed tool, full page, own H1
/<sub-intent>/        distinct sub-jobs of the primary tool
/blog or /guides/     only if it answers a real query — never filler
```

**Internal linking rules:**

- Every tool page links to **every other tool page** — the site is small enough that a flat
  graph beats a hierarchy.
- Descriptive anchor text using the target phrase. Never "click here", never bare URLs.
- A persistent tool nav in the header or a footer grid, crawlable as real `<a href>`.
- Breadcrumbs on every non-home page, marked up (see schema).
- **No orphan pages.** Every URL reachable within 2 clicks of the homepage.

## 4. On-page: titles, meta, headings

**Title tag** — the single highest-leverage on-page element:

- Primary keyword **first**, ≤ 60 characters, no brand suffix on the homepage if it costs
  you the keyword.
- Pattern that works for tools: `Mouse Tester — Test Buttons, Scroll & Double-Click Free`
- Every page a **unique** title. No templated duplication.

**Meta description** — does not rank, but drives CTR, which does:

- 140–160 characters, states what the tool does *and* the differentiator.
- Put the privacy angle in: "Runs entirely in your browser. Nothing uploaded."
- Front-load the verb: "Test your…", "Check any…", "Extract…".

**Headings:**

- Exactly one `<h1>` per page, containing the primary phrase, visible above the fold.
- `<h2>` per genuine section, using secondary phrases naturally.
- **Never skip levels.** h1 → h2 → h3, no jumps.
- Headings describe content, not decoration. No `<h3>` used for styling.

**URL slugs:** lowercase, hyphenated, short, contains the target phrase, no dates,
no stop words, no trailing IDs.

## 5. Content below the tool

The tool is what ranks; **the content is what stops a competitor outranking you.** Bare tool
pages lose to tool pages with real depth.

Write, in this order, *below* the working tool:

1. **What this tool does** — 2–3 sentences, plain language, contains the primary phrase.
2. **How to use it** — numbered steps, genuinely short.
3. **How to read the result** — what a pass/fail actually means. This is the section
   incumbents skip and it is the easiest place to be better.
4. **Common problems and fixes** — the long-tail goldmine. Each subheading is a real query.
5. **Device / browser / OS specifics** — where behaviour differs.
6. **FAQ** — see the mandatory research step below.

**Rules:** no keyword stuffing, no AI-slop padding, no "In today's digital world". Every
paragraph must answer something a real person typed. If a section exists only for word count,
delete it.

### ⚠ MANDATORY: FAQ questions come from Google's "People Also Ask" — never from imagination

**Do this for every site, every time. Do not write a single FAQ question from your own head.**

PAA is Google publishing, verbatim, the questions it associates with your keyword. Inventing
questions instead means writing an FAQ for demand that does not exist — and forfeiting the PAA
box, which is a real SERP position you can win.

**How to gather them:**

1. Open the five synonym SERPs for this site — **the ready-made US-geo links are in
   `BRIEF.md` under "Target keyword cluster"**. Open them in an incognito window.
2. On each SERP, find the **People Also Ask** box and **expand every question**. Each
   expansion generates new ones — keep going until they start repeating or drift off-topic.
3. Record **15–25 questions verbatim**, exactly as Google words them. Do not paraphrase.
4. Supplement from the same pages: **"Related searches"** at the bottom, Google autocomplete
   for `<keyword> why/how/what/can/does`, and the cluster in `BRIEF.md`.
5. Repeat per locale once you add languages (§14) — **PAA differs by country and language.**
   German PAA is not translated US PAA.

**Then:**

- Cluster near-duplicates, keep **10–15** distinct questions.
- Use Google's exact phrasing as the `<h3>`. It is what people type.
- **Answer completely in the first 2–3 sentences** — that is the extractable passage for both
  PAA and AI answers (§16).
- Mark up with **FAQ JSON-LD**.
- Keep the raw list in the repo (e.g. `docs/paa-research.md`) so it can be re-checked when
  rankings move.

**Sanity check:** if a question in your FAQ did not come from PAA, related searches, or
autocomplete — delete it or go find the real version.

## 6. Schema — be honest about what it does

Implement as JSON-LD in `<head>`:

| Type | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `WebApplication` (or `SoftwareApplication`) | Entity clarity: what this thing is, `applicationCategory`, `browserRequirements`, `offers` with price 0 |
| `BreadcrumbList` | **Still earns visible breadcrumb rich results** |
| `FAQPage` | Entity understanding + AI citation |
| `WebSite` + `Organization` | Ties the pages into one entity |

**Honest caveat:** Google removed `HowTo` rich results and restricted `FAQPage` rich results
to authoritative government/health sites in 2023. Do **not** implement these expecting stars
or dropdowns. Implement them because structured data helps Google and AI systems understand
and cite the page. **Never fake `aggregateRating`** — it is a spam violation and a manual
action risk. *(Rich-result eligibility changes without notice — verify at build time.)*

Validate every page with Google's Rich Results Test and Schema.org validator before launch.

## 7. Technical baseline

- **One canonical per page**, self-referencing. No duplicate content across www/non-www,
  http/https, trailing-slash variants — pick one and 301 the rest.
  **See §17 for the Astro config that prevents this, and for what each GSC indexing status
  actually means.**
- `robots.txt` allows everything except genuinely private paths. Link the sitemap from it.
- **Sitemap — submit BOTH the index and the child.**
  `@astrojs/sitemap` generates **two** files: `sitemap-index.xml` (the index) and
  `sitemap-0.xml` (the actual URL list). Very large sites also get `sitemap-1.xml` etc.
  **`sitemap.xml` does not exist — do not look for it.**

  | Submit to GSC + Bing | Why |
  |---|---|
  | `/sitemap-index.xml` | Future-proof — automatically covers any numbered file added later |
  | `/sitemap-0.xml` | **Per-sitemap indexation stats.** Submitting only the index gives one aggregate row and hides which URLs actually got indexed |

  - `robots.txt` references the **index only**:
    `Sitemap: https://yourdomain.com/sitemap-index.xml`
  - Only 200-status, canonical, indexable URLs. Accurate `lastmod`. No parameters.
  - **Filename is irrelevant to SEO.** Google treats all naming conventions identically. Two
    rules: keep it **static** (never generate changing filenames — Google tracks what it has
    already crawled), and keep robots.txt, GSC and the real file all naming the same thing.
    **Do not use `filenameBase` to rename it — there is no benefit and it invites drift.**
  - **Once locales exist (§14):** if you want per-locale indexation visibility, split the
    sitemap per language and submit each child individually. Optional — it needs custom
    `@astrojs/sitemap` config, and these sites are small enough that one child file is normal.
- **HTTPS everywhere**, HSTS, no mixed content.
- Custom 404 that links to every tool. No soft-404s.
- No `noindex` leaking to production. Check before every deploy.
- `hreflang` **only if** you build genuine country pages — the geo split in `BRIEF.md`
  tells you whether that is justified. Most of these clusters are US-first.
- Server response < 200ms TTFB (Cloudflare edge handles this).
- No JS-dependent content — Google renders JS, but rendering is queued and delayed. **The
  page must be meaningful in raw HTML.**

## 8. Responsive and design consistency

- **Mobile-first indexing** — Google ranks what it sees on mobile. Build mobile first, then
  widen.
- Tool fully usable at **320px** width. Test at 320 / 375 / 768 / 1024 / 1440.
- Touch targets ≥ 44×44px with ≥ 8px spacing.
- No horizontal scroll at any width. Wide tables/code get their own `overflow-x` container.
- Identical component system across all 19 sites — same spacing scale, type scale, colour
  tokens, button styles. Consistency is a build-speed decision as much as a design one.
- Dark mode via `prefers-color-scheme`, tokens defined once.

## 9. Accessibility — it is also SEO

Semantic HTML is what Google parses. An accessible page is a machine-readable page.

- Real landmarks: `<header> <nav> <main> <footer>`. One `<main>`.
- Every control a real `<button>` or `<a>` — never a clickable `<div>`.
- Labels on every input. `aria-live` for tool results so screen readers announce them.
- Visible focus states. Full keyboard operability — the tool must work without a mouse.
- Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 body, ≥ 3:1 large text and UI.
- `alt` on every meaningful image; `alt=""` on decorative.
- Run `accesslint:audit` and fix everything before launch.

## 10. AI Overview and AI Mode citability

*(Google-specific. For ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini / Perplexity see **section 16, AEO** — they source differently and ranking on Google does not carry over.)*

Even though tool queries are protected, the *supporting content* queries are not — and
citations drive branded search.

- Answer each FAQ question **in the first two sentences** below its heading. AI systems
  extract passages, not pages.
- Use unambiguous factual statements, not marketing prose.
- Keep entities explicit: name the tool, the file type, the hardware, the standard.
- Tables and lists get extracted more reliably than paragraphs.
- Keep the raw HTML clean — content buried in JS or deep nesting is skipped.

## 11. Google Search Console — setup, current features, and what it will not tell you

### Setup

1. **Use a Domain property, verified by DNS TXT.** Not a URL-prefix property. A Domain
   property covers `www`/non-`www`, `http`/`https`, every subdomain **and every `/es/`,
   `/pt-br/` locale subdirectory** in one place — and DNS verification survives changing host.
2. **Verify the real domain at launch, not `pages.dev`.** The staging URL is `noindex`, so a
   property on it just reports "Excluded by noindex" and teaches you nothing.
3. **Submit both `sitemap-index.xml` and `sitemap-0.xml`** immediately after verification. The index is future-proof; the child is what gives you per-sitemap indexation data in the Sitemaps report. Submitting only the index costs you that visibility.
4. **Turn on email alerts** — manual actions and security issues are the two things you must
   never discover late.
5. **Verify Bing Webmaster Tools too.** Free, five minutes, and it is the path into ChatGPT
   (see §16). Not optional for this portfolio.

### Performance → Generative AI (launched 3 June 2026)

Google now reports **AI Overviews and AI Mode separately** from normal search — the first time
this has been visible.

| | |
|---|---|
| Where | **Performance → Generative AI** |
| Metric | **Impressions only** |
| Breakdowns | page, country, device, date (hourly to monthly) |
| **Not** provided | **clicks / CTR, the user's prompt, and position** |
| Rollout | staged, began in the UK — **may not appear on a new property yet** |

**Two things to keep straight:**

- It shows *that* you surfaced in Google's AI, not *what for*. No prompt-level data exists, so
  you cannot reverse-engineer which questions triggered you.
- **It covers Google only.** ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity report nothing — those
  need the manual monthly check in §16.

### Other current features worth using

| Feature | Use for this portfolio |
|---|---|
| **Custom annotations** on Performance charts | Mark launch date, each locale added, each redesign. Across 19 sites this is how you attribute a traffic change to a cause months later — **do this from day 1** |
| **Branded vs non-branded query filter** | Tracks whether your own brand moat is forming — the thing coolors and iLovePDF used to become unbeatable |
| **AI-powered report configuration** | Natural-language filter building; saves time, changes nothing strategically |
| **24-hour / hourly view** | Only useful right after a launch or a fix; ignore day to day |
| **Platform properties** (Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube) | Not relevant unless you build a video presence — note that Gemini leans on YouTube (§16) |

### Things to keep in mind — where GSC misleads

- **Data lags 2–3 days.** Do not judge a change same-week.
- **"Average position" is an average across queries and is close to meaningless.** A page at
  #3 for one term and #50 for another reports ~#26. **Always filter to a single query before
  reading position.** This is the single most common misreading of GSC.
- **Impressions count being *on* the page shown, not being seen.** A #40 result that nobody
  scrolled to still counts.
- **The UI caps exports at 1,000 rows.** Use the API or Looker Studio when the site grows.
- **Re-requesting indexing does nothing.** Once is enough; repeat submissions do not speed
  anything up.
- **Pages report "why not indexed" is the highest-value screen on a new site** — Discovered
  not indexed, Crawled not indexed, Duplicate without canonical each mean something different
  and each has a different fix.
- Check **International Targeting** for hreflang errors once locales exist (§14).

**What to judge months 1–6 on** — not raw traffic:

1. **Average position trend per cluster.** 60 → 35 → 22 is success at zero clicks. Flat for
   three months is the failure signal.
2. **Count of keywords with any impressions** — should grow weekly.
3. **CTR where already top-10.** Under 3% at position 5–8 = the title/description is wrong,
   not the ranking.
4. **Time to first page-1 keyword.**

## 14. Internationalisation — rank globally, not just US

The research measured everything `gl=us` because that is where **value per visit** is highest.
That was right for *ranking* the portfolio and wrong as a *ceiling*. Non-US is additive.

Proof from the research itself: `key-test.ru` earns **741.4K visits with no US presence at
all** — more than the US keyboard winner. `split pdf` is 53% India. `merge images` is 76%
India. `youtube thumbnail downloader` is 66% Pakistan. On `speaker test`, India carries **5x
the US volume**.

### The honest caveat

Non-US traffic is worth **$0.05–0.15/visit** against **$0.30–1.10** for US/UK/CA/AU. Global
multiplies visits, not revenue, at the same rate. It is still clearly worth doing — the tool
is already built, so a new locale is marginal cost — but do not model 5x traffic as 5x revenue.

### Most "non-US" traffic in this data needs NO translation

India, Pakistan, Philippines, Nigeria, Malaysia, Singapore, UK, Canada, Australia all search
**in English**. A single strong English page already serves them. Translating for India is
wasted effort.

**Split the work:**

| Bucket | Action |
|---|---|
| English-speaking markets (IN, PK, PH, NG, MY, SG, UK, CA, AU) | **No translation.** One canonical English page. Optionally `en-GB` / `en-IN` variants only if spelling genuinely differs (`colour` vs `color` — real for the colour tools) |
| Genuinely non-English (BR, ID, VN, TR, DE, ES/LatAm, FR, JP, RU, KR, IT, PL) | **Real translated pages** |

**Pick locales from the data, not a blanket list.** The incumbent's top-5 countries in
`BRIEF.md` tell you which languages this specific cluster actually needs. Ship 2–3 locales
first, measure, then extend.

### URL structure — subdirectories

```
/                English (x-default)
/es/             Spanish
/pt-br/          Portuguese (Brazil)
/id/             Indonesian
```

**Subdirectories, not subdomains or ccTLDs.** One domain accumulates all the authority, and
at 19 sites ccTLDs are financially absurd. Astro has built-in i18n routing — use it.

### hreflang — this is where almost everyone breaks it

- Every localised page needs hreflang tags for **every** locale **including itself**
  (self-referencing is mandatory).
- Tags must be **reciprocal**. If `/es/` points to `/`, then `/` must point to `/es/`.
  One-way tags are ignored entirely.
- Always include `x-default` pointing at the English version.
- Use correct codes: `pt-BR` not `pt-br`-as-language, `es-419` for LatAm Spanish, plain `es`
  if you are not distinguishing.
- Put them in `<head>` **or** the sitemap — not both, and never conflicting.
- Each localised page gets its **own self-referencing canonical**, pointing at itself, never
  at the English version. Canonical + hreflang fighting each other is the classic failure.

### Never auto-redirect by IP

Googlebot crawls predominantly from the US. IP-redirect and Google only ever sees English —
your translated pages never get indexed. Serve the requested URL, and offer a **language
switcher** with real crawlable `<a href>` links.

### Translate everything, not just the UI

Title · meta description · H1 and all headings · body content · FAQ · alt text · schema
`name`/`description` · OG tags · the 404 page. A half-translated page ranks for nothing.

### Locale keyword research, not literal translation

The searched phrase is rarely the dictionary translation. Germans search `tastatur test`.
Brazilians search `teste de teclado`. Run the target phrase through the same
`serp.py`-style check with `gl=de`, `gl=br`, `gl=id` and target **what people actually type**,
then write the page around that phrase.

### Machine-translation risk — real

Google's spam policy covers **scaled content abuse**. Bulk raw MT across 19 sites x 10 locales
is exactly the pattern it targets. Mitigate:

- Ship **few locales, done well** rather than many done badly.
- Review every translated page for natural phrasing before publishing.
- Keep the tool UI strings machine-translated if you must — but the **content sections must
  read as if a person wrote them.**
- Never auto-generate locales you cannot review.

### Why global is a genuine edge, not an afterthought

**Almost everyone optimises for US English. That makes non-English SERPs measurably softer.**
The research proves these clusters are **fragmented by geography** — different sites win the
same query in different countries:

| Query | US winner | Non-US winner |
|---|---|---|
| `keyboard test` | keyboardtester.com | **key-test.ru** — 741.4K, owns SEA, *absent from the US* |
| `speaker test` | onlinemictest.com (5K vol) | **audiocheck.net** — #1 in India, **5x the volume** |
| `youtube thumbnail download` | — | youtube-thumbnail-grabber.com, **481.5K**, India 55% |

Geographic fragmentation is the same signal as competitive fragmentation: **nobody owns the
whole thing.** A site that ranks in 6 languages competes against a different, weaker set of
incumbents in each one.

### Sequencing — launch multilingual, expand monthly

Do **not** wait for English to rank first. That concedes a year of the softest SERPs available.

| Stage | Locales |
|---|---|
| **Launch** | English + the **top 2–3 non-English markets** from the incumbent's country split in `BRIEF.md` |
| **Month 2 onward** | +2 locales per month, each verified with in-market keyword research |
| **Ceiling** | Stop adding when a new locale's cluster is under ~2K volume, or when you cannot review the translation quality |

Three locales done properly beats ten done with raw machine translation — the constraint is
**review capacity, not ambition**. Expand as fast as you can genuinely check the output.

### Added pre-launch checks (once locales exist)

- [ ] hreflang reciprocal and self-referencing on every page, `x-default` present
- [ ] Each locale has its own self-referencing canonical
- [ ] No IP-based redirect; crawlable language switcher
- [ ] Locale keyword verified in-market, not translated literally
- [ ] Every element translated including schema and alt text
- [ ] GSC International Targeting report shows zero hreflang errors

## 15. Multi-page architecture — MPA, never SPA

**Every route is a real URL that returns complete HTML on a full page load.** No client-side
router, no scroll-to-section pretending to be navigation, no single page with tabs standing in
for pages.

### The accurate reason

Googlebot *does* render JavaScript — evergreen Chromium, since 2019. The claim that it "only
sees the root div" is out of date. But rendering is a **second pass**: queued, delayed by
hours to days, and not guaranteed under crawl-budget pressure. Bing and the AI crawlers
(GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot) are materially worse at it.

**So: never depend on rendering for anything you need indexed.**

### The distinction that matters for these builds

| Must be JavaScript | Must be in the initial HTML |
|---|---|
| The tool itself — a mouse tester cannot be static | Every `<h1>`/`<h2>`, all body copy, the FAQ |
| Result rendering, canvas, device APIs | Every internal `<a href>`, nav, footer, breadcrumbs |
| | `<title>`, meta description, canonical, hreflang, JSON-LD schema |

Interaction is JS. **Everything Google reads is HTML.** View source with JS disabled: the page
must still be a complete, meaningful document.

### Required separate pages

Each its own URL, own `<title>`, own H1, linked from the footer on every page:

```
/about/          who runs this, why it exists — a real E-E-A-T signal
/contact/        real reachable method
/privacy/        REQUIRED for AdSense approval
/terms/          terms of use
/404             custom, links every tool
```

**AdSense will not approve a site without a privacy policy**, and about/contact pages are
standard approval criteria. Build them before applying, not after being rejected.

### Astro specifics

- Astro is MPA by default — this is why it is the portfolio stack. Do not fight it.
- **Do not enable `<ClientRouter />` / View Transitions.** Each URL still serves full HTML so
  it is not an SEO problem, but it ships router JS and adds INP risk for zero ranking benefit.
  Full reloads on a static edge-hosted site are already instant.
- One `.astro` file per route under `src/pages/`. Shared layout, not shared page.
- `client:visible` or `client:idle` on the tool island only — never `client:load` on anything
  above the fold, it wrecks INP.

### Verify before launch

```
curl -s https://yoursite.com/about/ | grep -c "<h1"     # must be 1, from raw HTML
```

Then in Chrome DevTools: disable JS, reload every route. Content, headings and links must all
still be there. Finally, GSC **URL Inspection → View Crawled Page** on 3 routes — confirm the
raw HTML Google fetched contains your content.

## 16. AEO — getting recommended by ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity

### The goal is different for a tool site

Content sites want to be **quoted**. A tool site wants to be **recommended**.

An AI cannot test someone's mouse or open their SVG. But when a user asks *"how do I check if
my mouse is double-clicking?"*, the model should answer with the steps **and name this site**.

That means the model must know four things, stated plainly on the page:

1. The tool exists and what **exactly** it does
2. It is **free, no signup, runs in the browser**
3. Who made it and that it is trustworthy
4. Which specific problems it solves

### Two paths, only one of which you can optimise

| Path | How it works | Can you influence it? |
|---|---|---|
| **Live retrieval** — ChatGPT Search, Claude with search, Perplexity, AI Overviews | Crawled at query time | **Yes. This is the target.** |
| **Training data** | Baked in months ago | Only indirectly, by existing widely over time |

### Engine-by-engine — they behave differently

| Engine | Sources from | What that means here |
|---|---|---|
| **ChatGPT** | Bing index + partnerships | **Bing Webmaster Tools is not optional** |
| **Google AI Overviews** | ~76% overlap with organic top-10 | Ranking on Google *is* the AEO work |
| **Perplexity** | rewards freshness | Real `dateModified`, keep pages current |
| **Claude** | most conservative | Needs clear authority and unambiguous claims |
| **Gemini** | leans on Reddit and YouTube | Presence beyond your own site matters |

> **Only ~12% of ChatGPT citations overlap with Google's top 10** (vs 76% for AI Overviews).
> **Ranking #1 on Google does not get you into ChatGPT.** Treat Bing indexing and AEO as
> separate work, not a by-product of SEO.

### robots.txt — allow the retrieval bots explicitly

Training crawlers and retrieval crawlers are **different user-agents**:

- **Training:** `GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `Google-Extended`
- **Retrieval / search:** `OAI-SearchBot`, `Claude-SearchBot`, `PerplexityBot`

**Blocking retrieval bots removes you from AI answers entirely.**

For an ad-funded free tool there is no IP to protect and everything to gain from reach —
**allow all of them.** Be explicit rather than silent:

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /
User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /
User-agent: Claude-SearchBot
Allow: /
User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /
User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /
User-agent: Bingbot
Allow: /
```

> **⚠ Cloudflare gotcha — check this before launch.** Cloudflare offers one-click AI
> crawler blocking and has applied it by default on some plans/domains. If it is on, your
> `robots.txt` is irrelevant — the bots never reach you. **Verify AI bot blocking is
> DISABLED** in the Cloudflare dashboard for every site in this portfolio.

### llms.txt — cheap, unproven, do it anyway

A proposed standard: a markdown file at `/llms.txt` mapping your key pages for AI consumers.
**Google has said it does not use it**, and support elsewhere is claimed but not confirmed.
It costs ten minutes. Ship it; do not build a strategy on it.

### What actually earns the recommendation

Reported AEO weighting puts **FAQ schema quality ~20%**, **answer-first formatting ~19%**,
and **statistical density ~16%** *above* backlinks and keyword density — which suits a
no-backlinks strategy well.

- **Answer first, always.** The first two sentences under any heading must contain the whole
  answer. Models extract passages, not pages.
- **State the differentiators as facts**, not marketing: "Free. No account. Nothing is
  uploaded — processing happens in your browser." Those exact sentences get repeated by models.
- **Be specific and numeric.** "Detects double-clicks under 80ms" beats "detects issues".
- **Name the entity consistently** — same site name everywhere, in schema `name`, in copy.
- **Tables and lists extract more reliably** than prose.
- Cover **"alternative to X"** and **"X vs Y"** honestly — heavily surfaced in AI answers.

### Presence beyond your own site

Gemini leans on Reddit and YouTube; ChatGPT weights partnerships. You cannot rank your way
into those.

**This is not backlink building and must not become spam.** Answer questions genuinely on
Reddit, Stack Exchange or forums **only where your tool is honestly the right answer**, with
disclosure that you built it. One useful honest answer beats a hundred drops, and the fake
version gets you banned and poisons the brand.

### Measuring it

1. **Monthly manual check.** Ask ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity the 5 target questions
   for this tool. Record whether you are named. This is the only direct measure.
2. **Server logs / Cloudflare Analytics** — watch for the AI user-agents above actually
   fetching pages.
3. **Referral traffic** from `chatgpt.com`, `perplexity.ai`, `claude.ai`.

### Added pre-launch checks

- [ ] `robots.txt` explicitly allows all AI retrieval + training bots
- [ ] **Cloudflare AI crawler blocking confirmed OFF**
- [ ] Bing Webmaster Tools verified, sitemap submitted (this is the ChatGPT path)
- [ ] `/llms.txt` published
- [ ] Every FAQ answer complete within its first two sentences
- [ ] "Free / no signup / in-browser" stated as plain factual sentences
- [ ] Baseline recorded: what each of the 4 models says today for your target questions

## 17. GSC indexing problems — prevent them, do not fix them later

Most indexing damage is caused at build time by four config decisions. Get them right in the
first commit and almost none of this report ever goes red.

### First: know which statuses are NOT problems

| Status | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Alternate page with proper canonical tag** | ✅ **Healthy.** This is what Google reports for a correctly canonicalised duplicate — your hreflang locale pages will sit here. It means the canonical worked |
| **Excluded by 'noindex' tag** | ✅ Expected. Your `pages.dev` URLs live here permanently (§7) |
| **Page with redirect** | ✅ Expected for intentional redirects |

**Do not "fix" these.** They are the system working.

### The four config decisions that prevent most problems

```js
// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';
import sitemap from '@astrojs/sitemap';

export default defineConfig({
  site: 'https://yourdomain.com',   // 1. REQUIRED - canonical + sitemap URLs
  trailingSlash: 'never',           // 2. pick ONE and never change it
  integrations: [sitemap()],
});
```

1. **`site` is mandatory.** Without it, canonicals and the sitemap generate wrong or relative
   URLs. Set it to the **custom domain**, never `pages.dev` — even while building on `pages.dev`.
2. **`trailingSlash` must be explicit.** Left ambiguous, `/about` and `/about/` both return
   200 and you have manufactured a duplicate of every page on the site. This is **the single
   most common cause** of `Duplicate without user-selected canonical` on Astro sites. Pick one,
   then make **canonical, sitemap, internal links and redirects all agree**.
3. **www vs non-www — pick one and 301 the other** at Cloudflare. Both resolving is a
   site-wide duplicate.
4. **Every page self-canonicals**, including every locale (§14). A locale page canonicalising
   to English deletes it from the index.

### The genuinely broken statuses

| Status | Real cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Duplicate without user-selected canonical** | No canonical tag, or `/page` and `/page/` both live | Self-canonical everywhere + fix `trailingSlash` |
| **Duplicate, Google chose different canonical than user** | Your canonical was **ignored** — pages too similar, or sitemap/internal links contradict the canonical | Make the pages genuinely distinct; ensure canonical, sitemap and internal links all name the same URL |
| **Crawled – currently not indexed** | Quality judgement. Google fetched it and decided it adds nothing | Real depth (§5). Thin tool pages with no content land here |
| **Discovered – currently not indexed** | Crawl budget or predicted low value | Fewer URLs, better internal linking, better content |
| **Soft 404** | Returns 200 but looks empty to Google | **High risk here:** a tool page whose content is all JS renders empty in the raw HTML. See §15 |
| **Indexed, though blocked by robots.txt** | Blocked from crawling but indexed anyway, with no snippet | Never use `robots.txt` to hide a page. Use `noindex` — Google must be able to *crawl* it to *see* the noindex |
| **Redirect error** | Chain or loop | Single-hop redirects only |

### Tool-specific trap: query parameters

Several tools in this portfolio can produce shareable result URLs
(`?url=`, `?hex=`, `?v=`). If those are ever linked or crawled, **you have created an infinite
crawl space** — every input is a new URL, all near-duplicates.

Pick one before shipping any shareable-result feature:

- **Canonical every parameterised URL to the clean page** (`/redirect-checker/`), or
- **`noindex` parameterised URLs** via `X-Robots-Tag` / meta, or
- **Keep state out of the URL entirely** (fragment `#` is not crawled) — simplest, and the
  default choice unless sharing results is a real feature.

Never let parameterised URLs into `sitemap-index.xml`.

### Other prevention

- **`/index.html` must not be reachable alongside `/`.** Check after the first deploy.
- **Sitemap contains only 200-status, self-canonical, indexable URLs.** No redirects, no
  noindexed pages, no parameterised URLs. A sitemap that disagrees with your canonicals is a
  direct cause of "Google chose different canonical".
- **Do not `Disallow` in `robots.txt` what you want deindexed** — see the table above.

### Checking

After launch, use **URL Inspection** on 3 pages: home, a secondary tool page, and a locale
page. Confirm "User-declared canonical" matches "Google-selected canonical" on each. When
those two differ, that is the problem — everything else is noise.

*(GSC's Page Indexing report had multi-week data delays in June–July 2026. If the numbers look
stale or frozen, verify with URL Inspection before assuming a real regression.)*

### Added pre-launch checks

- [ ] `site` set to the **custom domain** in `astro.config.mjs`
- [ ] `trailingSlash` explicit; the wrong variant 301s or 404s — never 200s
- [ ] www/non-www: one canonical host, the other 301s
- [ ] Every page self-canonicals, every locale included
- [ ] `curl -I` the `/index.html` form of the homepage — must not return a bare 200
- [ ] Sitemap: only 200, canonical, indexable URLs; no parameters
- [ ] Decision made and implemented for query-parameter URLs

## 18. Everything that can hinder SEO — and how to prevent it

A single prevention list. Most items link to the section with detail; the ones written out in
full are the ones **not covered elsewhere** and most likely to bite this specific portfolio.

### A. Self-inflicted by monetisation — the most likely wound

Ads are how this site earns, and badly implemented ads are the fastest way to destroy the
rankings that produce the earnings.

| Risk | Prevention |
|---|---|
| **AdSense Auto Ads** insert slots unpredictably at runtime | **Do not enable Auto Ads.** Place every unit manually. Auto Ads are the #1 cause of CLS on ad-funded sites |
| Ad loads shift the page | **Reserve the exact height of every slot in CSS** before the ad arrives. An unreserved slot is guaranteed CLS |
| Ads delay the tool | Load ad JS **after** the page is interactive. Never in `<head>`, never blocking |
| Ad above the tool | **Nothing goes above the tool.** The tool is the reason the visitor came and the reason Google ranks you |
| Ad density outnumbers content | Content must dominate. A page that is mostly ads is a Core Update casualty |
| **Intrusive interstitials** — popups, overlays, full-screen prompts on mobile | **Never.** This is an explicit Google demotion, not a soft signal |
| Consent banner blocking content | Google requires a **certified CMP for EEA/UK ad traffic**, and you are targeting globally (§14). Keep it a **small bottom bar**, never a full-screen blocker |

**Analytics: use GA4, linked to AdSense.** You need **revenue per page**
(Monetization -> Publisher Ads) to know which pages and which sites actually earn — no other
free tool provides it, and it is the feedback loop this whole portfolio runs on.

A cookieless alternative would avoid a consent banner, but **AdSense already requires a
certified CMP for EEA/UK traffic**, so the banner exists regardless and that argument does not
apply here. Load GA4 **after interactive** so it costs nothing in INP.

**Neither choice affects rankings.** Google Analytics is not a ranking factor — this is purely
a measurement decision.

**Sequencing:** apply for AdSense **after** traffic exists. Ads on a zero-traffic site earn
nothing and only add CLS risk during the phase where you are establishing Core Web Vitals.

### B. Content risks

| Risk | Prevention |
|---|---|
| **Keyword cannibalisation** — two of your own pages competing for one query | One page per *distinct intent*, never per variant (§3). If two pages rank for the same term, merge them |
| **Thin pages** — a bare tool with no content | 800–1200 words of genuine depth below the tool (§5). "Crawled – currently not indexed" is the punishment (§17) |
| **Scaled content abuse** — many sites, one owner, AI-assisted content | Mitigated by building each site as a **separate project** with its own design, structure and freshly written copy — but not eliminated. Every page must answer something a real person typed. No filler, no padded word counts. If a paragraph exists to hit a target, delete it |
| Near-duplicate pages *within* a site | Each absorbed tool gets genuinely different content, not a find-and-replace of the last one |
| Near-duplicate **sites** across the portfolio | Different design language, layout and copy per site. Never clone the previous build |
| Machine-translated locales shipped unreviewed | §14 — few locales done well, each reviewed |

### C. UX signals that feed back into ranking

| Risk | Prevention |
|---|---|
| **The tool is broken** | The single worst SEO outcome. A visitor who bounces in 3 seconds tells Google everything. **Test on real hardware, on the live URL, on mobile, before every launch** |
| Tool needs a click to start when it could auto-start | Ask for permission/input only when genuinely required; otherwise show a working result immediately |
| Requires signup | **Never.** No account, ever (§ stack rules) |
| Slow on mid-range Android | Your global traffic is not on flagship phones. Test throttled, not on your dev machine |
| Layout breaks at 320px | §8 |

### D. Technical — cross-references

| Risk | Section |
|---|---|
| Duplicate content, canonical conflicts, GSC index statuses | **§17** |
| `pages.dev` duplicating the live site | **§7** — permanent `_headers` noindex |
| JS-only content invisible to crawlers, soft 404s | **§15** |
| Core Web Vitals failure | **§2** |
| Missing/duplicate titles and meta | **§4** |
| Broken schema | **§6** |
| hreflang errors, wrong canonicals per locale | **§14** |
| AI crawlers blocked (incl. Cloudflare's default blocking) | **§16** |
| Orphan pages, no internal links | **§3** |
| Accessibility failures | **§9** |

### E. Migration risk — `pages.dev` to custom domain

The one moment this portfolio is most likely to lose rankings.

- **Canonical points at the custom domain from day one**, while still on `pages.dev` (§17).
- **`site` in `astro.config.mjs` is the custom domain**, never `pages.dev` — set before the
  first deploy.
- **Never let `pages.dev` get indexed** in the first place — permanent `_headers` (§7). If it
  never entered the index, there is nothing to migrate.
- Verify GSC by **DNS TXT**, so the property survives the host change.
- Submit the sitemap only **after** the custom domain is live.

### F. Ongoing — things that rot

| Risk | Prevention |
|---|---|
| Links break, tools stop working after a browser update | Re-test the tool on real hardware quarterly. A Chrome release can break a device API |
| Content goes stale, Perplexity deprioritises you | Keep `dateModified` real and update pages when the underlying thing changes (§16) |
| Silent CWV regression from a new feature | Baseline `claude-seo:seo-drift` at launch, compare monthly |
| Competitor ships something better | The incumbents in `BRIEF.md` are moving — five were caught growing during this research. Re-check yours at the month-4 checkpoint |

### Added pre-launch checks

- [ ] **Auto Ads OFF**; every ad slot manually placed with reserved height
- [ ] No ad, popup or overlay above the tool; no mobile interstitials
- [ ] Ad and analytics JS loads after interactive
- [ ] Consent banner (if any) is a small non-blocking bar
- [ ] Tool verified working on **real hardware**, on the live URL, on mobile
- [ ] No two pages target the same query
- [ ] Every page answers a real query — no filler written to hit a word count

## 19. AdSense approval — required pages, done properly

Ads are the revenue. A rejection costs weeks, and repeat rejections for the same reason are
harder to recover from than getting it right once.

### ⚠ The tension with a tool site — read this first

Reviewers expect **roughly 15-20 substantive pages** of genuine content. A bare tool site with
a homepage and four legal pages **will likely be rejected as "low value content"** — the most
common rejection reason there is.

Google does not publish a hard page count, but the practical bar is real. Reaching it:

| Page type | Count |
|---|---|
| Primary tool page (800-1200 words below the tool) | 1 |
| One page per distinct sub-intent (§3) | 4-8 |
| Genuine guides answering real queries — from PAA research (§5) | 3-6 |
| About, Contact, Privacy, Terms | 4 |
| **Target** | **15+** |

**"AI-generated content without editorial oversight typically fails review."** Every page must
be read and corrected by a human before applying. This is not optional and it is exactly the
failure mode this portfolio is exposed to.

### Timing — do not apply on launch day

- **Apply after real traffic exists**, not at launch. Ads on a zero-traffic site earn nothing
  and only add CLS risk while you establish Core Web Vitals (§18A).
- **Domain age helps.** There is no official six-month rule, but new domains are reviewed
  harder. Applying 2-3 months post-launch is a better bet than week one.
- The site must be **complete**. No placeholder pages, no "coming soon", no dead links.

### The four pages — what each must actually contain

Every one gets its own URL, its own `<title>`, its own `<h1>`, and a **footer link on every
page of the site**.

**`/privacy/` — the only strictly mandatory one**

A generic template is a rejection risk and a legal one. It must be accurate for *this* site:

- What data is collected, by whom: **Google AdSense** (third-party cookies, personalised ads),
  **Google Analytics 4**, Cloudflare.
- A link to **Google's own "How Google uses information from sites"** page.
- How users opt out — Google Ad Settings, browser cookie controls.
- **GDPR/EEA:** the certified CMP you use, and how consent is withdrawn (§18A).
- **CCPA** if you take US traffic.
- **Children's privacy / COPPA** statement.
- Data retention, and a **real contact address for privacy requests**.
- **State the in-browser processing truthfully.** "Files you open are processed entirely in
  your browser and are never uploaded to our servers." That is true for most of these tools,
  it is a genuine trust signal, and reviewers notice specificity.

**`/about/` — establishes authorship and expertise (E-E-A-T)**

The page most often written as filler and most often the reason for rejection.

- **Who built this** — a real person or entity, named. Not "we are a team of passionate
  developers".
- **Why it exists** — the actual problem it solves.
- **How the tool works technically** — which browser API, what it measures, what it cannot.
  Demonstrates genuine expertise rather than claiming it.
- **What its limits are.** Stating what the tool cannot detect builds more trust than
  overclaiming, and is honest.

**`/contact/` — must be genuinely reachable**

- A **working email address**. Set up **Cloudflare Email Routing** to forward to Gmail so the
  address is on the site's own domain.
- Or a form — but a form alone with no address is weaker.
- Say what you respond to and roughly how fast. Do not promise what you will not do.

**`/terms/` — not strictly required, but standard and useful here**

- **No warranty / use at own risk.** This matters more than usual: these are *diagnostic*
  tools. Someone may conclude their hardware is faulty based on your output. Say plainly that
  results are indicative, not a professional diagnosis.
- Acceptable use, IP ownership, limitation of liability, governing law.

**Plus `/404` and `/500`** — both custom, both linking to every tool (§15).

### Before applying — checklist

- [ ] 15+ substantive pages, every one genuinely useful
- [ ] **Every page human-reviewed**, not raw AI output
- [ ] About names a real person/entity and explains how the tool works
- [ ] Privacy policy names AdSense, GA4, cookies, CMP, COPPA, and the real contact address
- [ ] Contact email works — send a test to it and confirm delivery
- [ ] All four pages footer-linked from every page, each with unique title + h1
- [ ] Custom 404 and 500
- [ ] Zero placeholder content, zero dead links, zero "coming soon"
- [ ] Mobile layout correct, navigation obvious
- [ ] Site has real traffic and has been live for at least a few weeks
